description: Plutonium is a silvery-gray actinide metal with atomic number 94 that tarnishes when exposed to air and forms a dull coating when oxidized. It normally exhibits six allotropes and four oxidation states, and reacts with carbon, halogens, nitrogen, silicon, and hydrogen. The element is radioactive and was first synthesized in 1940-1941 by deuteron bombardment of uranium-238 at the University of California, Berkeley.
uses: Plutonium-239 and plutonium-241 are fissile isotopes used in nuclear weapons and nuclear reactors. Plutonium-238, with a half-life of 87.7 years, is used as a heat source in radioisotope thermoelectric generators that power some spacecraft. Plutonium oxides are preferred for applications such as nuclear fission reactor fuel.
characteristics: At room temperature, plutonium has a silvery appearance but oxidizes quickly to dull gray, though yellow and olive green are also reported. It has a low melting point of 640 °C and an unusually high boiling point of 3,228 °C. Unlike most metals, plutonium is not a good conductor of heat or electricity, and it increases in density by 2.5% when it melts, which is unusual behavior for a metal.
